WHEREAS, the role of an independent Civil Aviation Authority, which provides fof the regulation
and promotion of civil aviation, and which fosters its safe evelo I's-considered vital to the
socio-economic progress of the State of Eritrea;
WHEREAS, the State of Eritrea is Signatory to the Convention on International Civil Aviation
(Chicago Convention, signed at Chicago on 7 December, 1944), and is obligated to adopt
measures to ensure safety through conformity with international standards in its safety oversight
obligations; and
WHEREAS, a fundamental element of national safety oversight is legislation establishing and
empowering a civil aviation authority in the State of Eritrea, and the promulgation of specific
operating regulations for civil aviation;
PART I
GENERAL
CHAPTER I
Article I. Repeal
The Civil Aviation Proclamation No. 130/2003 is hereby repealed and replaced by this
Proclamation.
In the application of this Proclamation, unless the content otherwise requires, the following
terms and phrases shall have the following meanings:
Territory of the State of Eritrea: The land areas and territorial waters adjacent thereto and the
airspace above such land areas and territorial waters.

Civil Aviation Authority: The Civil Aviation Authority charged with its terms of reference and
competencies.
Director General: The Director General appointed and mandated to oversee the civil aviation
affairs of the State of Eritrea.
The Convention: The Convention on International Civil Aviation, signed in Chicago on
7/12/1944 and to which the State of Eritrea acceded on 17/11/1993 and any amendments to the
Convention adhered to by the State.
The Organization: The International Civil Aviation (ICAO) Organization which was established
under the Convention.
Aircraft: Any machine that can derive support in the atmosphere from the aerodynamic
reactions of the air, other than the reactions of the air against the Earth's surface.
State Aircraft: Military aircraft and aircraft used solely in the service of the State including but
not limited to police, immigration, agricultural, surveying and customs.
Operator: A natural or legal person engaged in the operation of an aircraft whose flight crew
are subject to his orders, whether for his own account or on behalf of a third party.
State of Operator: The State in whose territory the operator maintains his principal place of
business or permanent residence.
Air carrier: A natural or legal person engaged in the operation of an air service(s) to carry
passengers, mail or cargo.
Aerodrome: A defined area on land or water including any buildings, installations and
equipment intended to be used either wholly or in part for the use of aircraft on arrival or
departure or movement on the surface.
Airfield: Any surface that may be used for landing or take-off which does not have all the
necessary facilities for public use like aircraft hangars, catering facilities or facilities for receiving
passengers and loading cargo
International airport: An airport designated by the competent authorities for arrival and
departure of international air traffic, where the formalities incident to customs, immigration,
public health, quarantine (animal and plant) and similar procedures are carried out.
Maneuvering area: That part of an aerodrome used for take-off, landing and taxiying of aircraft,
excluding aprons.
Aerodrome traffic: The aircraft traffic and movement of other vehicles in the maneuvering area
of the Aerodrome as well as all aircraft flying in the vicinity of the aerodrome.
Aerodrome Traffic Zone: airspace with defined dimensions designated around the aerodrome
to protect traffic of such aerodrome.

Airport Operator: A natural or legal person engaged in the oper tie-rramt-a€l inistration of an
airport either by himself or through his subordinates. \ SIr. y 0
\
Pilot-in-command: The pilot who holds a valid flying icens~, and charged wi h the safe
conduct and safety of an aircraft in flight. I'
Flight Crew Member: A licensed crew member holding a v "d licenserand caged with d4ties
essential to the operation of an aircraft in flight.
Crew Member: A person assigned by an operator to duty on an aircraft during a flight duty
period.
Flight time: The total time from the moment an aircraft starts moving under its own power for
the purpose of take-off until the moment it comes to a complete stop at the end of a flight.
Prohibited area: An airspace of defined dimensions declared by the competent authorities,
within the territory of the State, within which the flight of aircraft is prohibited.
Restricted area: An airspace of defined dimensions declared by the competent authorities,
within the territory of the State where the flight of aircraft is restricted under certain conditions.
Danger zone: airspace with defined dimensions, declared by the competent authorities, where
activities that pose danger to aviation, at certain times, take place.
Scheduled air service: A group of flights by aircraft for the public transport of passengers, mail
or cargo for remuneration or hire, which is open to the public in accordance with a published
schedule and clear regularity and frequency.
Scheduled international air service: Any regular air service whose point of departure or
destination is situated in the territory of another State other than the territory of the State of
Registry
Scheduled domestic air service: A regular air service the point of departure of which is
situated in the territory of a state and the destination of which is situated in the territory of
another state.
Joint registration. A registration system under which aircraft are listed in a dedicated record,
whether unified or separate, other than the national register.
International registration: A registration system under which aircraft are registered in an
organization possessing an international legal personality.
Common mark: A mark designated by the Organization for the mark registration authority in
order to register aircraft of an international or joint-operation airline, other than for the purpose of
national registration
Common mark registration authority: The authority entrusted in whole or in part with non-
national registration, where records are maintained for aircraft of an international or joint-
operation airline
International airline: An airline having an international legal personality and engaged in
operating international air services.

Joint Operation Airline:. An airline that is formed by a group of states or legal persons
affiliated to such states in accordance with their domestic legislation, which operates
international air services.
Acrobatic night: Maneuvers intentionally performed by an aircraft involving an abrupt change
in its attitude, an abnormal attitude or an abnormal variation in speed.
Accident: An occurrence associated with the operation of an aircraft which takes place from
the time any person boards the aircraft with the intention of flight until such time as all such
persons have disembarked, in which:
a person is fatally or seriously injured as a result of being onboard the aircraft, or coming in
direct contact with any part of the aircraft; or
Excluded are the serious injuries which do not result directly from the operation of the aircraft,
including:
Incident: An occurrence, other than an accident, associated with the operation of an aircraft
which affects or could affect the operational safety.
Air Operator's Certificate: A general authorization issued by the Civil Aviation Authority
containing detailed regulatory provisions and conditions and according to which the operator of
an aircraft or the air carrier may perform, within the determined activities, for such operations in
the territory of the state, for a specified period of time; it shall also contain the cases where it
would be suspended or revoked.
Certificate of Airworthiness: A document issued by the Civil Aviation Authority attesting to the
airworthiness of an aircraft for a specific period, provided that the operator complies with the
conditions specified in such document to perform one or more specific aerial operations.
Search and Rescue: Any assistance provided to an aircraft, even by way of information, if it
encounters an incident, danger or difficulties, or if there is suspicion or fear regarding its safety
This includes assistance to persons on board.

CHAPTER"
SOVEREIGNTY AND POWERS OF THE STATE
Article 4.Sovereignty
The State has complete and exclusive sovereignty over the airspace above its territory.
Article 5.Scope of Application
1.The provisions of this Proclamation apply to the following:
Article 6.Provisions of International Conventions
The provisions of the Convention and other conventions and agreements in force to which the
State is a party shall apply to the State of Eritrea in accordance with the terms and conditions
contained therein.
Article 7.Supervision of Civil Aviation Affairs
The Civil Aviation Authority shall be responsible for implementing the provlSlons of this
Proclamation. The Minister shall supervise all civil aviation affairs in the State and shall take the
necessary decisions for the implementation of this Proclamation.
The Director General shall be responsible for the exercise of all powers and the discharge of all
duties of the Authority and shall have control over all personnel and activities of the Authority.
The Director General may elect, employ, and appoint such officers, employees, consultants,
attorneys, and agents as shall be necessary to carry out the provisions of this Proclamation, and
define their authority and duties. No officer, employee, or attorney of the Authority shall have a
monetary interest in or over any stocks and shares and bonds of any air transport enterprise.

The Director General may, subject to such regulations, supervision, and review as may be
prescribed, authorize the performance by any officer, employee, or administrative unit under his
jurisdiction of any function under this Proclamation.
The Director General is authorized to delegate any assigned powers and duties to any properly
qualified private person, subject to such regulation, supervision, and review as may be
prescribed. The Director General shall, however, ensure that such functions are not delegated in
such a way that air operators, aerial work or a general aviation operators and maintenance
facilities, in effect, regulate themselves.
Implement and enforce this Proclamation, as well as related national laws and regulations;
propose amendments to this Proclamation to conform to changes that enhance aviation
development and safety;
Investigate, examine and report on the operation and development of commercial air services
in, to or from Eritrea;
Provide for the publication of all reports, orders, decisions, rules, and regulations issued under
this Proclamation in such form and manner as may be best adapted for public information and
use;
Promote air transport services by such means as the Director General considers appropriate,
and undertake such other activities in relation to air transport services as the Director General
considers appropriate, or as the Minister of Transport and Communications directs;
Plan, develop, construct, maintain and operate domestic and international aerodromes and
establish and provide other facilities and services relating to air transport services;
Undertake and cooperate with persons undertaking such projects, technical research, study or
investigation as, in the opinion of the Director General shall promote the development of air
transport services;
Promote fair competition and efficient market conditions in the air transport sector of the national
economy;
Promote the development of national human resources for the aviation industry within Eritrea
through the establishment and certification of aviation training centers;

Develop, issue and maintain regulatory documents to implement Air Navigation and Air
Transport systems including but not limited to Communications, Navigation and Surveillance/Air
Traffic Management in Eritrea in conformity with ICAG standards and recommended practices;
Formulate, develop, issue, update regulatory documents and legal notices for the registration,
certification and licensing of aircraft, aerodromes, personnel, air transport services and related
facilities;
Establish and provide facilities and services for the collection, publication or dissemination of
information relating to air transport services and enter into arrangements with any person
natural or legal or branch of government for the collection, publication and dissemination of that
information;
Issue, renew, validate, endorse, suspend or revoke licenses, permits and certificates in accordance
with the provisions specified in the regulatory documents;
Inspect and grant approval for maintenance organizations, aviation training institutions, air traffic
services (equipment and facilities), aerodrome, air operators and air travel agencies;
Inspect and license civil aviation training centers which promote the aviation human resources of
the State;
Prevent the unlawful interference of aircraft operations by anyone, and the placement or removal of
any objects which, in the opinion of the Director General, may jeopardize continued safe operation
of flights;
Develop and implement mechanisms for aviation emergency services which prevent and minimize
the occurrence of accidents and incidents;
Coordinate, promote and facilitate the establishment of and implementation a National Aviation
Security Program;

Identify Air Traffic Services Routes to be used within and across Eritrea and prescribe the
conditions of their use;
Establish, provide, maintain and enhance a system of Air Traffic Management to ensure the safety,
economy and security of national and international air navigation within and across the State.
For the purposes of providing aviation weather services that will ensure the safety, regularity
and efficiency of aircraft operation, enter into arrangements with any branch of the Government
of Eritrea that is capable of, and responsible for providing those services or, where those
arrangements cannot be made, enter into arrangements with any person natural or legal with
respect to the provision of those services in such form and manner and at such places as the
Director General considers necessary;
Control and manage all aircraft and equipment necessary for the conduct of any services in the
State;
Control and regulate the manufacture, assembly, possession, use, operation, sale, import and
export of any aircraft and spare parts;
Act consistently with any obligations assumed by the State under any international treaty,
convention and agreement that may be in·force between the State and any foreign countries;
Take such action as may be necessary to protect, by international regulation or otherwise, the
rights of the State in international air transport services;
Cooperate or enter into administrative, bilateral or multilateral arrangements with civil aviation
authorities of other governments, foreign states and international organizations with respect to
any matter pertaining to air transport services;
Coordinate and supervise the review, initiation, regulation and approval or revocation of fares,
tariffs and rates on civil aviation and non-civil aviation services and facilities;
Regulate and control aviation services (fuel supply, travel agencies, handling agencies, aircraft
concessionaires), including airport and air navigation service charges and related insurance
premiums.

The Authority shall have the powers to perform such acts, to conduct such investigations, to
issue and amend such orders, and to make and amend such general or special rules,
regulations, and procedures pursuant to and in accordance with the provisions of this
Proclamation, as the Director General shall deem necessary to carry out the provisions of, and
the exercise and performance of the powers and duties assigned under this Proclamation. The
Authority shall have the power to utilize land and other facilities, provided, however, that due
compensation is paid for buildings, crops and plants so removed by the Authority as deemed
necessary.
Article 8.Use ofAircraft in Emergencies
In cases of disasters such as floods and earthquakes etc., the Minister may, upon
recommendation by the Director General, decide that any and all aircraft present at Eritrean
airports be used on a temporary basis against fair remuneration.
Article 9.Inspection ofAircraft, Denial of Departure and Seizure of Documents
The Director General may order the inspection of any aircraft, deny its departure or seize any
documents related thereto in exercising his authority to oversee the implementation of this
Proclamation.
Article lO.Customs, Security, Health and Agricultural Quarantine
Customs, Aviation Security, Health and Agricultural Quarantine officers may inspect any aircraft
or any person or cargo on board an aircraft, in accordance with this Proclamation and
regulations applicable in the State. Such inspection shall be conducted without causing any
unreasonable delay under the supervision of the Civil Aviation Authority, without the latter's
interference in the inspection process.
Article ll.Compliance with Arrival and Departure Regulations
The operator of any aircraft arriving at or departing from the territory of the State shall comply
with the regulations in force, including regulations pertaining to arrival and departure,
immigration, customs and health and agricultural quarantine.
CHAPTER III
GENERAL FLIGHT PROVISIONS
Article l2.Flight Authorizations and Permits
No aircraft may be operated within the territory of the State except in accordance with a formal
authorization or permit issued by the Director General under the terms as may be specified by
him or in accordance with:
an effective bilateral air services agreement concluded between the State and
any state to regulate such air services.

Article 13. Conditions to be fulfilled by Aircraft Operating within the Territory of the State
No aircraft may be operated within the territory of the State unless it fulfills the following
conditions:
a) The aircraft is registered in its State or registered in conformity with international
or joint registration regulations;
b) The aircraft is airworthy as may be established by a valid certificate of
airworthiness issued or validated by the State of Registry, or issued or validated
by a state delegated for this purpose by the State of Registry in conformity with
established international rules;
c) The aircraft distinctly displays its nationality and registration marks in accordance
with established rules;
d) The aircraft carries such equipment and instruments as may be determined by
the State of Registry as well as the Civil Aviation Authority;
e) The flight crew members are in possession of valid licenses, issued or validated
by the competent authorities of the State of Registry or issued or validated by a
state delegated for this purpose by the State of Registry in conformity with the
established international rules;
f) The aircraft flight crew complies with the approved flight manual in respect of
their duties to insure the safety of the aircraft and the passengers and cargo on
board.
g) The aircraft is insured in respect of its crew, passengers and cargo on board and
in respect of third parties on the surface in accordance with the relevant
established rules.
The Director General may exempt aircraft engaged in technical test flights or training or
instruction flights from one or more of the above-mentioned conditions.
Article 14. Radio Equipment and their Use in Aircl aft
1. No aircraft operating in the territory of the State may be equipped with any radio
equipment without authorization by the comp''3tent authorities in the State of Registry or
any other state delegated for this purpose by the state of Registry under arrangements
made in accordance with the established internat"onal rules.
2. Such equipment may not be used for purposes other than air navigation and, in
accordance with the established conditions, such use shall be exercised by the flight crew
members.
Article 15.Transport of Dangerous Goods
Unless otherwise specifically authorized by the Director General, it is prohibited to transport
weapons, ammunitions and explosives and any articles that may be used for military purposes
in the state or foreign aircraft operating in the State.

No Eritrean or foreign aircraft operating in the State may transport any dangerous objects the list
of which is issued by decision of the Director General, unless otherwise authorized under the
relevant terms and conditions as may be determined in this connection.
Article 16. Aerial Photographic Equipment
No aircraft fitted with aerial photographic equipment may operate within the territory of the State
or use such equipment without prior authorization by the Director General and in conformity with
the relevant prescribed conditions
Article 17. Responsibility of the Pilot-in-command
The pilot-in-command shall be responsible for the operation and safety of the aircraft and its
occupants during the flight and may take the necessary measures to maintain order on board.
He must also ensure compliance with the applicable rules in this regard.
Article 18. Interference with the Flight Crew and Tampering with the Aircraft
No person may, without official authorization, interfere with the work of any member of the flight
crew or impede the exercise of his duties; and no person may tamper with any of the parts or
equipment of the aircraft or act in any manner that might endanger the safety of the aircraft, its
flight crew or its passengers.
PART II
AERODROMES AND AIR NAVIGATION FACILITIES
CHAPTER IV
AERODROME CONSTRUCTION, MANAGEMENT AND UTILIZATION
Article 19. Construction, Operation and Preparation of Aerodromes and Airfields
No aerodromes or airfields may be constructed, equipped, utilized or operated in the State
without prior authorization by the Director General.
Article 20. Legal Status of Aerodromes and Facilities
All aerodromes, facilities, buildings, systems and equipment and telecommunication stations
and beacons that are affiliated to the Civil Aviation Authority are public utilities and are
considered public property.
Article 21.Regulating, Supervising and Monitoring Airports
The Civil Aviation Authority shall regulate, supervise, monitor and audit airports affiliated to the
Authority, and shall supervise other airports and ensure compliance with rules, regulations of
operation mandated to, including conclusion of ATS agreements with other CAAs in respect of
the coordination of air traffic control
Article 22. Supervision of Persons and Personnel at Airports
Without prejudice to the provisions of the previous Article, the Airport Manager shall supervise
all airport personnel regardless of the body to which they are affiliated in all matters that may

ensure the proper operation of the airport. To this end, the airport manager shall directly
investigate violations to take the necessary action thereon.
Article 23.Types of Airports
The Director General shall determine the type and category of each airport, including
international airports in particular, in agreement with the competent authorities.
Article 24.Use of Airports
All aircraft shall use the designated airports and shall comply with the relevant laws, rules and
regulations. No aircraft may land in other airports except in emergency situations or by virtue of
an authorization from the Director General;
Each aircraft entering in the territory of the State shall land at a designated international airport,
unless only authorized to transit. Each international flight departing from the territory of the State
shall take off from an international airport.
Subject to the procedures applied in international airports, the Director General may exempt
certain aircraft, because of the nature of their operations and other considerations, from
complying with the above requirements. Such authorization must designate the airport of
landing and departure as well as the route and instructions to be followed.
If an aircraft while entering, departing or transiting the airspace of the State is forced to land at
other than the international airports of the State, the pilot-in-command shall immediately advise
the nearest local authority and furnish the aircraft's log book, general declaration or any other
document upon request. In such a case, the aircraft may not take-off, have its load transferred
or passengers leave the place where it landed before obtaining an authorization from the
Director General and taking the required measures. In all cases, the pilot-in-command shall
provide evidence of the reasons of the forced landing.
CHAPTER V
AIR EASEMENT RIGHTS
Article 25.Aerial Easement Rights
Special easement rights, to be named aerial easement rights, are established to safeguard air
navigation safety and the proper functioning of its systems, in order to:
a) Prevent the establishment or removal of any buildings, facilities, installations, pillars,
cables, plantations or other obstacles regardless of their kind or height, in the vicinity of
airports and navigational aids; and
Article 26.Limits of Easement Rights
The Director General shall determine the scope and extent of aerial easement rights and the
areas where they are imposed to ensure air navigation safety and to protect persons and
property in accordance with the established international rules and regulations in this regard.
Article 27.Installations in the Areas Covered by Easement Rights
It shall be prohibited to erect, build or establish any obstacles in the areas covered by the aerial
easement rights, nor make any modification in the nature or scope of the use of land subject to

easement, without prior permission by the Director General and in accordance with the
prescribed conditions.
Article 28.Installations and Facilities that May Affect Air Navigation Safety
No light or radio beacon shall be established without the permission of the Director General.
The Director General may take the necessary measures to suspend, remove or modify any
lighting apparatus that may be wrongly confused with lighting systems in support of air
navigational aids. He may also impose any necessary restrictions on facilities producing smoke
or other materials in a manner that may affect visibility in the vicinity of airports or affect air
navigation safety;
Any person who owns or uses fixed or mobile electrical apparatuses or facilities or installations
that may cause interference with the radio equipment or air navigational aids shall strictly apply
the measures determined by the Director General to eliminate such interference.
Article 29.Compensation for Enforcement of Easement Rights
A fair compensation shall be paid for violation of easement rights.
CHAPTER VI
PROTECTION OF AIRPORTS, AIRCRAFT AND NAVIGATIONAL AIDS
Article 30.Security Regulations and Instructions at Airports
The Civil Aviation Authority shall, in coordination with the other competent authorities, establish
regulations and instructions and take the necessary measures to safeguard security at the
airports of the State and protect the safety of persons, aircraft and navigational aids.
Article 31.Carriage of Weapons and Dangerous Objects on Board Aircraft
No person on board an aircraft may, without authorization, carry any weapon or inflammable
material or any other objects that may be used in an act of sabotage, violence or threat during
the flight.
If it is necessary to carry an unloaded weapon, inflammable material or any other objects that
could be used in any of the afore- mentioned acts, the person lawfully holding such material
shall deliver it to the operator's representatives before embarking on the aircraft; it shall be
placed in a safe place to which the passengers cannot have access, and returned to the person
at the end of the flight.
Article 32.Control ofAirmail
All mail and mail parcels sent by air shall be carried in accordance with the established postal
security regulations, subject to the provisions of the international conventions acceded to by the
State.
CHAPTER VII
AIRCRAFT NOISE
Article 33.Noise Level Determination
The Director General, shall determine the maximum allowable noise level for aircraft operating
into airports of the State. He shall also determine the flight level and speed and engine power of

aircraft as well as any other conditions that would ensure maintenance of the above-mentioned
noise level at the points of measurement that he may designate.
The Director General shall issue noise certificates for aircraft on the register of the State in
accordance with the rules, regulations and requirements established.
1. Rules under which the Director General may issue noise certificates for aircraft
on register as provided for inArticle 34 of this Proclamation;
2. Noise rules and requirements in respect of aircraft operating in the territory of the
State.
PART III
AIRCRAFT
CHAPTER VIII
AIRCRAFT REGISTRATION
Article 34.Nationality and Registration Marks
No aircraft may operate in the territory of the State unless it carries its national and registration
marks in accordance with the laws of the State of Registry or in accordance with the
international or joint registration system. However, the Director General may authorize a non-
registered aircraft to fly or land for purposes of technical testing or any other purposes in
accordance with the terms of the authorization.
Article 35.Determination of the Nationality and Registration Marks
The nationality mark of Eritrean aircraft consists of E3-followed by three Latin unadorned letters
(E3-AAA)
The Director General shall determine the registration mark, which shall consist of three Latin
unadorned letters. The nationality mark shall be placed before the registration mark with a dash
separating the two.
Article 36.Aircraft Register
The Director General shall maintain a national regis):8rwhere aircraft are listed. For an aircraft to
be registered therein, it shall satisfy the following requir\.~ments:
That the aircraft is not listed in the register of another state or is subject of an
international or joint registration;
That it is held by persons holding the Eritrean nationality, under a lease-purchase
contract or a leasing contract entitling them to hold the aircraft for a minimum
period of two years.

Article 37.Enjoyment of Eritrean Nationality
An aircraft that is listed in the register referred to in the previous Article shall be considered as
holding the Eritrean nationality and shall carry its nationality and registration marks.
Article 38.Contents of the Aircraft Register and Certificate of Registration
a) The register referred to inArticle 34 above shall contain the following information:
Statement of the documents and contracts proving the ownership and operation
of the aircraft.
The director General shall issue the certificate of registration upon completion of the
necessary formalities.
Article 39.Removal from Aircraft Register
An aircraft may be removed from the aircraft register in the following cases:
The owner or lessee of an aircraft shall notify the Director General of any change to the
conditions covered by this Article and shall surrender the certificate of registration of the
aircraft.
Article 40.Change or Death of the Aircraft Owner or Lessee
In case of a change of the aircraft owner or lessee, the person in whose name the aircraft is
registered or his estate shall notify the Director General with such change or death, and the date
thereof, in order to enter such information in the aircraft register.

Article 41.Aircraft Owned by Foreigners
The Minister, upon recommendation by the Director General, shall issue a decision stipulating
the regulation, conditions and modalities for the registration of aircraft owned by persons who do
not hold Eritrean nationality and who are residents of the State.
Article 42.Joint Registration Rules
For purposes of joint registration of aircraft owned by an international or joint airline of which the
State is a member, the following requirements shall be taken into consideration:
1. An agreement shall be concluded between the Civil Aviation Authority of the State
and the Civil Aviation Authorities of the other member states airlines for the
establishment of ajoint register for the aircraft owned by the airline, provided that
such register shall be separate from the national register maintained by the State
in conformity with Article 34 of this Proclamation.
2. The joint register may be a consolidated or divided register under the following
conditions:
a. In case it is agreed to establish a consolidated register, the Civil Aviation
Authority shall agree with the Civil Aviation Authorities of the member states of
the airline, on a state among them which shall maintain the consolidated joint
register.
b. In case it is agreed to divide the joint register into several parts, the Civil
Aviation Authority shall agree with the Civil Aviation Authorities of the member
states of the airline, to maintain any part of the register;
c. An aircraft owned by the airline may be registered once either in the
consolidated register or in any part of the register. Such an aircraft may not be
entered in the register referred to in Article 34 of this Proclamation whether the
register or part thereof is held by the State;
d. All aircraft owned by the airline and entered in either the consolidated register or
part thereof shall display a uniform common mark;
e. Aircraft registered in conformity with this Article shall be deemed as holding the
nationality of each of the member states of the airline;
f. The State of Eritrea shall, jointly with th'9other member states of the airline, be
bound by the obligations established under this Proclamation for the State of
Registry as well as those established by international civil aviation conventions;
g. Without prejudice to paragraph c) above, if the State maintains the consolidated
register or part thereof, the Civil Aviation Authority shall perform the functions of
the State of Registry in accordance with the established provisions in this
regard, especially in respect of issuing certificates of registration and
airworthiness and flight crew licenses. In performing such functions, the State
shall implement its obligations in respect of itself and of all the member States of
the airline;

h. Provisions of Articles 36 and 37 of this Proclamation shall apply to joint
registration with the exception of paragraph (a), of Article 36.
Article 43.International Registration Rules
The following rules shall apply to the international registration of aircraft:
The Civil Aviation Authority shall agree with the Civil Aviation Authorities in the other member
states of the international airline to designate an international organization where the aircraft of
the airline may be registered internationally.
No international registration of aircraft owned by the airline may be made with more than one
international organization at the same time;
All aircraft owned by the airline and registered internationally must bear a uniform common
mark;
Aircraft subject to international registration in accordance with the provisions of this Article shall
be deemed as holding the nationality of all member states of the airline;
The State of Eritrea shall, jointly with the other member states of the airline, be bound by all the
obligations provided in this Proclamation for the State of Registry and all obligations imposed by
international civil aviation conventions;
The Civil Aviation Authority shall agree with the Civil Aviation Authorities in the other member
states of the airline to designate the agency that shall assume the functions of the State of
Registry, in accordance with the established regulations in this respect, particularly with regard
to the issuance of certificates of registration and airworthiness certificates and flight crew
licenses; and
The provisions of Articles 36 and 37 of this Proclamation shall apply to international registration,
with the exception of Paragraph (a), of Article 36.
CHAPTER IX
AIRCRAFT'S OWNERSHIP AND LEASE
Article 44.Legal Status ofAircraft and Transfer of Ownership
The aircraft is a mobile asset in connection with application of laws and Regulations in force in
the State. The aircraft ownership may be transferred by an official instrument and shall only have
effect vis-a-vis third parties upon its registration as provided for in Article 34 of this
Proclamation.
Article 45.Legal Actions
An aircraft on the register referred to inArticle 34 of this Proclamation may not be disposed of in
the interest of any foreigner, including by sale or mortgage without approval of the Director
General.

Article 46.Aircraft Leasing
No aircraft may be imported or leased by an Eritrean national or resident in Eritrea under a
lease-purchase arrangement without a special authorization by the Director General.
A leased aircraft may not be operated between the State and any other place abroad without
authorization by the Director General.
Article 47.Duties of the Lessee
The owner of an aircraft leased to another person shall remain jointly liable with the lessee for
any violation of the obligations legally placed thereon, unless otherwise agreed and provided the
lessee is competent to own an Eritrean aircraft and the agreement is registered asordained by the
Director General. In such a case, the lessee asthe aircraft operator, shall solely be liable for any
violation of the above-mentioned obligations. In this context, the leased the aircraft shall mean
to be an aircraft leased with its crew.
Article 48.Aircraft Leasing Rules
Decisions, rules and regulations issued under this Proclamation shall specify the provIsions
relating to wet and dry leases as well as the provisions relating to leasing of aircraft capacity,
including the duties and responsibilities arising from the charter of the aircraft or its capacity and
other relevant provisions.
Article 49.0peration of Leased Aircraft Not Holding the Operator's Nationality
No foreign airline may operate into, from and over the territory of the State of leased aircraft not
of the same nationality of such airline unless it receives a permit to do so from the Director
General and in accordance with the terms of such permit.
Article 50.Precautionary Seizure
The general rules in the Proclamation shall apply to the precautionary or executive seizure of
aircraft or its forced sale, without prejudice to any relevant provisions in the intemationallaws or
conventions to which the State is a party. The seizure shall be recorded in the relevant aircraft
register.
Article 51.Inadmissibility of Seizure on Patent Claims
An aircraft owned by a contracting state of the Convention may not be seized on the strength of
a claim by any person holding a patent in respect of the aircraft or any part thereof.
Article 52.Settlement of Seizure Disputes
Disputes relating to seizure of aircraft shall be settled promptly.
CHAPTER X
AIRCRAFT AIRWORTHINESS
Article 53.Certificate ofAirworthiness
1. No aircraft may be operated in the territory of the State unless it holds a valid certificate
of airworthiness issued or rendered valid by the competent authorities in the State of
Registry in accordance with the applicable laws, rules and regulations in force in that
State or any other state as may be delegated by the State of Registry in accordance with

the relevant international rules. The aircraft operator shall comply with the terms and
limitations shown in the certificate of airworthiness. The foregoing shall not apply to
aircraft flying in the territory of the State only for the purposes of testing, inspection or
any other operation related to the aircraft mechanical systems in accordance with the
conditions and restrictions established by the Director General.
2. The Director General may issue a certificate of airworthiness or render valid a certificate
of airworthiness issued by another state. He may also place any additional conditions or
restrictions for validations of such certificate.
3. Functions and duties related to the certificate of airworthiness in respect of an aircraft
registered in the State may, in accordance with the established international rules, be
transferred to another state if such an aircraft is operated under a lease, charter or
interchange agreement or any similar arrangement by an operator whose principal place
of business, or place of permanent residence if he does not have a place of business, is
in the territory of another contracting state. The provisions of this paragraph shall apply
to aircraft registered in accordance with Articles 40 and 41 of this Proclamation.
The State shall not be held liable in respect of the functions and duties so transferred to
the other state.
4. If the State of Registry transfers licensing functions and duties to the State in accordance
with the relevant international rules, the Director General shall issue a certificate of
airworthiness to any aircraft registered in another State if such aircraft is being operated
under a lease, charter or interchange agreement or any similar arrangements, by an
operator whose permanent residence is in the State,
The provisions of this paragraph shall apply to aircraft registered in accordance with
Articles 42 and 43 of this Proclamation.
This also applies to any aircraft registered in a contracting state and operated by an operator
whose principal place of business or residence is in the State, if the State of Registry has
transferred the functions and duties related to its certificate of airworthiness to the State in
accordance with the relevant international rules and bilateral arrangements in this regard.
Article 54.Aircraft Maintenance
a) No operator may operate an aircraft in the State unless it is maintained and serviced in
accordance with the. maintenance program approved by the Civil Aviation Authority
under the relevant rules and requirements.
b) The Civil Aviation Authority shall approve the national and foreign organizations engaged
in the maintenance and overhaul of aircraft registered in the State.
c) For the purposes of applying the provisions of this Article, any pilot-in-command of an
aircraft registered in the State that is engaged in commercial air transport flights or air
work, shall be required to record in the aircraft log book the following information:
2. Information on any technical defect or failure in any part of the aircraft or in any of
its equipment occurring during the flight. If no such defect or failure occurs, the

pilot-in-command shall record such fact in the register. The pilot-in-command
shall sign and date such record.
d) Keep the aircraft technical log book and maintain one copy of such record at operator's
head office.
e) The operator of an aircraft registered in the State shall keep maintenance documentation
for at least two years after expiry date of validity period. The Civil Aviation Authority may
require maintaining the same for a longer duration.
The operator of an aircraft registered in the State shall fit such aircraft with the systems and
equipment set forth in the Annexes of the Convention as may be applicable in the State.
The Director General may decide that any aircraft registered in the State be fitted with any
additional or special systems or equipment so as to guarantee the safety of the aircraft or crew
or to facilitate search and rescue operations.
The aircraft systems and equipment shall be installed in such a way as to facilitate replacement.
They shall also be maintained and calibrated to be readily usable.
The location of emergency equipment in every aircraft registered in the State shall be indicated
by clear markings, particularly the location and method of use of life vests and survival rafts.
In the installation or carriage of any equipment or systems on board an aircraft, care shall be
taken to avoid any danger for the airworthiness of the aircraft or any adverse impact on the
performance of the other safety-related equipment or systems.
Article 56.Other Technical Records
1. Other technical records that may be determined by the Director General shall be
maintained for all aircraft registered in the State.
2. These should include such data as may be determined by the Director General as soon
as circumstances permit following completion of the relevant work, and in any case, not
later than seven days following the date of completion of such work.
3. Upon entering such date in any of the technical records of the aircraft, reference may be
made to any other documents or records, in which case they shall be considered an
integral part of this record.
4. The aircraft operator shall be responsible for nlaintaining the aircraft technical records
and shall only dispose of them with permission of the Director General.
Article 57.Aircraft Weight
1. Each aircraft for which a certificate of airworthiness is issued or rendered valid by the
Director General shall be weighed and reweighed; its centre of gravity shall be
determined in such cases and such ways as may be determined by the Director
General.

2. The operator shall prepare the aircraft's loading schedule after weighing as may be
determined by the Director General.
3. The operator shall maintain the above-mentioned schedule and shall only dispose of it
by permission of the Director General.
Article 58.Airworthiness Inspection
The Director General, or any person acting on his behalf, may carry out inspections, tests or test
flights whenever he deems it necessary, to ascertain the airworthiness of the aircraft or any of its
systems or components as indicated in its certificate of airworthiness. Such procedures shall be
done at the expense of the operator. The Director General, or any person acting on his behalf,
may to enter any place at any time to perform any of such procedures, and may issue the
necessary instructions to the operator in this regard.
PART VI
RULES OF THE AIR
Article 59.Rules of the Air
The Director General shall issue the rules of the air and the regulations relating to the flight of
aircraft, protection of persons and property on the surface and utilization of the Eritrean
airspace.
Article 60.Compliance with Rules of the Air
The pilot-in-command is directly responsible for flying an aircraft in accordance with the
applicable rules of the air and may only depart from such rules in situations where this may be
imperative in the interest of safety. In such cases, he shall notify the competent authorities as
forthwith as soon as practicable.
Article 61.Air Routes and Corridors
The Director General shall designate air traffic services (ATS) routes that must be used by
aircraft entering into, departing from or transiting the territory of the State.
Article 62.Compliance with ATC Clearances and Instructions
The pilot-in-command shall comply with air traffic control (ATC) clearances and instructions and
may only depart from such instructions in emergency situations requiring immediate action. In
such situations, he shall notify the competent ATC unit as soon as practicable and shall obtain a
revised clearance as required.
Article 63.Air Traffic atAerodromes and Surrounding Area
The pilot-in-command of an aircraft operating on the aerodrome or in the surrounding area shall
comply with the regulations relating to the use of the aerodrome and air traffic rules.
Article 64.Flight Levels
1. No aircraft may fly below those levels that may be determined by the Director General,
except in emergency situations, or by authorization from the Director General.

2. Except for take-off and landing requirements or in case where a relevant authorization
has been granted by the Director General, no aircraft may fly over a city, a populated
area or a place of public assembly except at a level which would allow such aircraft, in
emergency situations, to land without causing any harm to persons or damage to
property on the surface. The minimum level to be observed shall be determined by the
Director General in such situations.
Article 65.Prohibited, Restricted and Danger Areas
1. The Director General may prohibit or restrict the flight of aircraft in the following
locations:
a) over designated areas of the State for military reasons or for public order
requirements or for reasons related to public security, or
b) In the territory of the State or part thereof, in exceptional cases for reasons
related to public order or public security.
2. The Director General shall designate danger zones.
3. If the pilot-in-command of any aircraft discovers that he is flying over a prohibited area,
he must notify the competent Air Traffic Control Unit and follow the latter's instruction
fully. If this is impossible, the pilot shall promptly effect landing at the nearest aerodrome
in the State away from the prohibited area. The pilot must provide the competent
authorities with a detailed report on this incident accompanied by the relevant
justifications.
4. The pilot of an aircraft receiving a warning by the competent authorities for flying over a
prohibited area shall immediately execute the instructions issued by such authorities,
failing which the competent authorities may take the necessary action to force the
aircraft to land upon such notification.
5. The prohibited and restricted areas shall be designated by decision of the Minister,
acting upon a recommendation by the competent authorities.
Article 66.Preflight Duties of the Pilot-in-command
Prior to the departure of a flight, the pilot-in-command shall perform the following duties:

In all cases, aircraft and aerodromes shall be used in accordance with the established
rules of the air and air traffic regulations.
PART V
LICENSING AND FLYING INSTRUCTION
Article 68.Flight Crew Licenses
1. A person acting as a member of the flight crew of an aircraft operating in the territory of
the State shall hold a valid license issued in accordance with the Proclamation, rules and

regulations in force in the State of Registry or any state authorized to do so in conformity
with the established international rules.
2. The Director General may withhold recognition of certificates and licenses issued to
nationals of the State by another State, for the purpose of flying in the territory of the
State.
Article 69.Licenses of Flight Crew of Eritrean Registered Aircraft
A person acting as a member of the flight crew of any aircraft registered in the State shall hold a
valid license issued or rendered valid by the Director General authorizing him to carry out his
duties.
Functions and duties relating to the issuance of licenses of flight crew of an aircraft registered in
the State may be transferred to another state if such an aircraft is operated, under a lease,
charter or interchange agreement or any similar arrangements, by an operator whose principal
place of business, or permanent residence if he does not have such place of business, is in
another contracting state.
The State shall not be liable in respect of the functions and duties which have been transferred
to the other state.
The Director General shall issue flight crew member licenses in respect of aircraft registered in
other states which are operated under a lease, charter or interchange agreement or any similar
arrangement by an operator whose principal place of business or permanent residence is in the
State, in case the State of Registry has transferred the licensing functions and duties in
accordance with the relevant international rules and bilateral arrangements.
Article 71.Terms and Requirements Related to the Issuance, Approval and Renewal of
Licenses and Ratings
The Director shall issue decisions related to the terms and requirements related to the issuance,
approval and renewal of licenses and ratings of the flight crew members.
Article 72.Exception to the Condition of Holding a License
A person not holding the required license may act as a pilot on an aircraft registered in the State
for the purpose of training or completion of tests for awarding, renewal or extension of validity of
a license, provided that the pilot-in-command holds the required license. In such a case, the
aircraft must only carry the following personnel:
The required license, for the purpose of this Article, is meant to be the licenses, certificates and
ratings that entitle the holder to perform duties aboard the aircraft during the relevant flight.

Article 73.Issuance, Approval and Renewal of Licenses Related to All Aeronautical Works
and Services
1. The Director General shall issue, approve and renew flying licenses and technical
licenses related to all civil aviation works and services in accordance with the terms of
their issuance, approval or renewal. Such terms shall be issued by decision of the
Director General.
2. The Director General shall issue the licenses mentioned in the previous paragraph upon
ascertaining that the applicant is qualified in terms of experience, knowledge, skills, age
and health, for the performance of duties under the relevant license. To this end, the
Director General may conduct any written or practical tests as he may see it fit.
3. The Director General may deny a request to issue, renew, approve or extend the validity
of any license falling within his competence, and may withdraw, suspend or cancel a
license if he finds out that the license applicant or holder fails to meet the required
standard or dropped below such standard or violated any provision of this Proclamation.
4. A license holder may not continue to perform the duties authorized under the license if
he becomes aware or has reason to believe that his state of health does not make him fit
to perform such functions either temporarily or permanently.
5. A flying license is considered suspended for at least twenty (20) days if its holder
sustains an injury or contracts an illness rendering him incapable of performing his duties
prescribed by the license.
In such cases the holder must advise the Director General in writing to allow the latter to
arrange for a medical examination established for the license that he holds.
Article 74.Maintenance Licenses and Privileges of their Holders
1. The Director General, shall determine the rules of the issuance, renewal and validity
period of licenses of maintenance technicians of the airframe, engines and equipment,
and also the privileges of the holders of such licenses as well as the terms of approving
foreign licenses.
3. The Director General shall approve the licenses referred to in paragraph (1) above
whenever they are issued by another state, such approval may be subject to certain
restrictions as may be determined by the Director General.
Article 75.Air Traffic Control Licenses and Privileges of their Holders
1. The Director General, shall determine the rules of the issuance, renewal and validity
period of licenses and privileges of air traffic controllers.
2. An air traffic controller may not work in any ATC unit unless he holds a valid license
including the relevant rating of such unit.
3. The Director General shall issue the licenses and privileges referred to in the above
paragraph.

Article 76.Cabin Crew Licenses
1. The Director General shall determine the rules for the issuance and renewal of cabin
crew licenses.
2. A person engaged as a member of the cabin crew on an aircraft operating in the territory
of the State must hold a valid license in accordance with the laws, rules and regulations
in force in the State of Registry.
Article 77.Dispatcher Licenses (Air Operations Officers)
1. The Director General, shall determine the rules for the issuance and renewal of flight
dispatchers (air operations officers).
2. A person engaged as a flight dispatcher (air operations officer) must hold a valid license
issued or rendered valid by the Director General authorizing him to perform his duties.
Article 78.Personal Flying Log
1. The Director General shall issue a decision concerning the personal flying log including
a description of its contents, duration and other related provisions.
2. Each member of the flight crew of an aircraft registered in the State and each person
flying for the purpose of instruction, completion of tests or to obtain or renew a license
must keep a personal flying log.
Article 79.Flight Instruction
No person may engage in flying instruction to qualify another person to obtain a flying license or
rating unless the instructor holds a valid license issued or approved by the Director General
authorizing him to act as pilot-in-command for the purpose of training and in the conditions
under which the training is being conducted. Such license must contain evidence of his
qualifications as an instructor on the same aircraft type. The Director General, shall determine
the requirements for the issuance or approval of flying instructor license.
Article 80.Flying Institutes and Clubs
1. The Director General shall issue the regulations and rules related to the activities of
flying institutes, centers and clubs.
2. No institute, center, club or any other entity may conduct flying instruction or training in
respect of aviation disciplines, or perform any other aeronautical activity without
authorization from the Director General and under the conditions of such authorization.
The Director General may suspend or revoke such authorization in case of any violation
of its conditions or infringement of the relevant laws and regulations.
PART VI
DOCUMENTS AND RECORDS
Article 81.Carriage of Documents and Records On Board Aircraft
1. Documents and records that must be carried on board aircraft engaged in domestic
flights, and exemption from the carriage of all or some of such documents and records

as well as the related requirements thereof shall be established by the executive
decisions of this Proclamation.
2. No aircraft may operate in the territory of the State unless it has on board the documents
and records that are provided for in the Convention and its Annexes and amendments
thereof, as well as the other documents and records that must be carried under the laws of
the State of Registry of the aircraft.
Article 82.Submission of Documents and Records
The operator, the pilot-in-command and any other competent person shall submit, at request, to
the Director General or officials of the Civil Aviation Authority as may be designated by a
decision of the Director General in conformity with the relevant established rules, any
documents, data or records as required by this Proclamation and its implementing decisions.
Article 83.Maintenance of Documents and Records
The aircraft owner or operator who ceases to use or operate the aircraft shall continue to
maintain its documents and records as well as the logs relating to the flight crew members, and
may not dispose of such documents without authorization from the Director General. Upon
transfer of the ownership or right of operation of an aircraft to another person, the owner or
operator shall deliver to the new owner or operator all the necessary documents and records.
The latter shall obtain the above-mentioned documents and records prior to operating the
aircraft. The relevant obligations of the former owner or operator shall be automatically
transferred to the latter owner or operator. If a member of the flight crew of an aircraft registered
in the State moves to another operator, the former operator shall deliver to the latter the relevant
records of that member as stipulated inArticle 102 (c) of this Proclamation.
Article 84.Revocation or Suspension of Documents
In case any certificate, license, approval, authorization, permit or other document which has
been issued by the Director General is revoked or suspended, the person to whom it has been
issued or its holder shall surrender itto the Director General.
Article 85.Ensuring the Safety of Documents and Records and Prohibition of Tampering
with or Misuse Thereof
1. No person shall commit any of the following acts:
a) Use any certificate, license, approval, permit or other document issued by the
Director General and subsequently revoked, suspended or amended or if its
holder was ineligible to carry it;
b) Lend any certificate, license, approval, permit or any other document issued by
the Director General or allow it to be used by any other person;
c) Make any false representation for the purpose of procuring for himself or any
other person any certificate, renewal or amendment of a certificate, license,
permit or any other document;
d) Damage or deform, or take part in damaging or deforming any record or
document required under this Proclamation, or modify or delete any of the data
or make false entries therein;

e) Delete any data from the load sheet or make false entries therein whether
intentionally or by negligence.
2. No person may issue any certificate, license or permit unless he is authorized to do so,
and in accordance with the required conditions in this regard.
3. All entries in any document or record shall be recorded in ink or any indelible material.
PART VII
COMMERCIAL AIR TRANSPORT OPERATIONS
CHAPTER XI
APPLICABLE LAWS, RULES AND REGULATIONS
AND SCOPE OF APPLICABLITY
Article 86.:.Scopeof Applicability
The provisions of this Part shall apply in the following cases:
1. Scheduled and unscheduled commercial air transport operations conducted by an
operator of an aircraft registered in the State by virtue of an authorization from the Civil
Aviation Authority granting the operator the right to conduct such operations between
two or more locations or within the territory of the State or between a location within this
territory and any location abroad, or between two locations abroad.
2. Any person employed by the operator who shall conduct any of the commercial air
transport operations indicated in paragraph 1 hereof.
3. Any person on board an aircraft engaged in any of the operations indicated in
paragraph.
Article 87.Applicable Laws, Rules and Regulations
The operator of an aircraft registered in the State shall take the following into consideration in
conducting its operation:

Article 88.Inspection of Commercial Air Transport Operations
Authorized personnel of the Civil Aviation Authority may enter any of the operator's locations for
the purpose of inspection and to monitor implementation of the operational specifications and
the local and international regulations and instructions as applied in the State. The Director
General has the right to suspend or revoke the authorization granted to the operator or suspend
any fight or air service if he considers that it is operated below the required level.
CHAPTER XII
ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF AIRLINES
AND AVIATION FACILITIES
Article 89.Procedures for the Establishment of Airlines and Aviation Facilities
Without prejudice to the regulations governing the instruments for the performance of economic
activities, no authorization may be granted to set up an instrument for the performance of
domestic or international commercial air transport or aerial work in the State without
authorization by the Director General.
Article 90. Licensing Operations of Airlines and Facilities
An operator fulfilling the requirements for establishing an airline or an aviation facility in the
manner indicated inArticle 89 may only commence operation upon obtaining the following:
1. An authorization from Director General after submitting documentary evidence for the
establishment of the airline or the facility.
CHAPTER XIII
SPECIFICATIONS OF PRELIMINARY OPERATION AND FLIGHTS
Article 91.0btaining Operational Specifications
An operator may only commence operations upon approval by the Director General of the
relevant operational specifications. Such specifications shall be considered an integral part of
the authorization granted to the operator and shall be duly applied.
Article 92.0perational Specifications
The operational specifications that are issued to the operator shall contain the following items:

Article 93.Approval of the Operational Specifications
1. The operator shall establish the operational specifications for its operations and present
them to the Director General.
2. The Aviation Authority shall review the specifications to insure compliance with the
established safety, regularity and efficiency standards, and shall approve them
accordingly.
3. The operational specifications may be modified at the request of the operator or if the
Director General finds it necessary to insure the required level of operational safety and
regularity.
Article 94.Preliminary Flights
1. The operator may not conduct a new air service or extend the operation of an existing air
service before carrying out one or more preliminary flights so as to demonstrate its
operational efficiency and safety in accordance with the provisions of this Proclamation
and its relevant regulations. The Director General may issue the necessary authorization
when he is satisfied that the required conditions have been met.
2. The operator may carry on board an aircraft on a preliminary flight only the persons
required for its operation and persons approved by the Director General. The operator
may carry mail or cargo during such flights.
3. The Director General may exempt an operator from carrying out any preliminary flights if
he had sufficient information and reasons confirming that such flights are not required, in
which case the first flight or flights would be carried out according to any such conditions
as established by the Director General for such flights.
CHAPTER XIV
OPERATIONS MANUAL
Article 95.0bligation to Develop an Operations Manual
The operator shall develop an operations manual for the use and guidance of flight crew
members and operations staff. The manual must describe the duties and responsibilities of the
flight crew members and operations staff and assist them in carrying out their duties so as to
ensure operational safety. The operator shall present the manual for approval by the Director
General. The manual must not contain any information or instructions that may be inconsistent

with the laws, rules and regulations applicable in the State or those issued by the Civil Aviation
Authority.
Article 96.Distribution of the Operations Manual
The operator shall distribute copies of all or parts of the operations manual and any
amendments thereof according to work requirements, to the agencies and persons engaged in
implementing its operations and supervising such implementation as may be decided by the
Director General.
Article 97.Approval of the Operations and Flight Manuals
Approval of the operations and flight manuals shall be in accordance with the rules established
by the Director General.
Article 98.0perations Manual
The Director General, shall issue the necessary regulations governing the development of the
operations manual, its contents, amendments and specifications
CHAPTER XV
FLIGHT CREW
Article 99.Composition
a) For all or some flights, the Director General may add one or more members to the flight
crew in addition to the crew composition as shown in the certificate of airworthiness or
flight manual, if he considers it necessary to insure flight safety.
b) In the composition of the flight crew for every flight, no one member may be charged
with the duties of two or more members of the flight crew.
c) The Director General may decide the minimum number of cabin crew who are entrusted
with duties related to safety and service of passengers on board.
d) For cargo planes, the Director General may decide the minimum number of loading
supervisors who are entrusted with duties related to the safety of the plane and its and
cargo.
Article IOO.Development of Training Programs
The operator shall develop training programs for members of the flight and ground crew
members to insure the proper performance of their duties. These programs shall be approved by
the Director General.
Article IOl.Flight Crew Testing
Each operator must ensure that the flight crew members and their ability to face emergency
situations in flight have been rested in practice thus confIrming the required ability in accordance
with the relevant applicable rules.

Article l02.Determination of Flying Time, Duty and Rest Periods
a) The Director General shall establish the regulations and instructions relating to the
maximum flying time, duty period and the minimum rest period for flight crew members.
b) Subject to the regulations and instructions referred to in the previous paragraph, the
operator shall ensure the period during which any member of the flight crew is required
to work on board an aircraft during which he is allowed to perform any other function or
duty as well as the rest period allowed, are such that the crew member is not exposed to
any stress, thus protecting his safety and that of the aircraft.
c) For each flight crew member, the operator must maintain a complete and accurate record
showing flying time and duty period, in accordance with the regulations and instructions
established by the Director General. Such records must be kept for at least 12 months
from the end of the duty period for each flight crew member.
CHAPTER XVI
AIRCRAFT EQUIPMENT AND SYSTEMS
Article l03.Aircraft Equipment and Systems
No aircraft may be operated unless it is fitted with the equipment and systems necessary for its
flight and navigation, whether in normal or emergency situations as provided for in its flight
manual and in the international regulations that are applicable in the State as well as any other
regulations and instructions issued by the Director General to ensure flight safety and
passenger convenience.
The Director General may exempt any aircraft from the requirement of carrying any of the
relevant equipment and systems if it considers that the aircraft is fitted with alternate equipment
and systems that give the required data or achieve the desired purpose.
Article 104.Aircraft Loading
The operator shall allow loading the aircraft only under the supervision of a load technician
whom he has provided with sufficient information and instructions in respect of the load
distribution and securing in order to ensure the following:

CHAPTER XVIII
FLIGHT OPERATIONS
Article 10S.Control of Flight Operations
The operator or its representative shall be responsible for controlling the flight operations of its
aircraft, thus insuring the conduct of such operations in accordance with the established safety
standards and the relevant laws, rules and regulations.
Article 106.Designation of the Pilot-in-Command
The operator must not allow a flight to be operated until it has designated one of its flight crew
as a pilot-in-command. The pilot-in-command shall be responsible for the safety of the aircraft
and its occupants. All persons on board the aircraft must implement any orders or instructions
issued by the pilot-in-command to insure the safety of the aircraft and the persons and property
on board, and to safeguard air navigation safety and regularity.
Article 107.Seating of Flight Crew Members
Each flight crew member must remain in his respective seat in the following situations:
Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph 1 of this Article, flight crew members may alternate
for the purpose of rest provided an additional member(s) is available on long haul flights.
Article lOS.Use of Controls
No person shall use the aircraft control systems during its flight other than a qualified member of
the flight crew designated by the operator accordingly.
Article l09.Cockpit Access
a) No person may enter the cockpit of the aircraft unless he is a member of its flight crew,
an inspector or controller designated by the Director General, or a person assigned by
the operator to carry out specific tasks. In such a case, the pilot-in-command shall be so
informed. This shall in no way limit the powers of the pilot-in-command in emergency
situations prevent entry of any person to the cockpit or remove a person from the cockpit
if he considers that such action is required for the safety of the aircraft.
b) Every person authorized to enter the cockpit shall have a passenger seat, unless he has
a seat in the cockpit. The number of persons present in the cockpit during take-off and
landing shall not be more than the number of seats in the certificate of airworthiness.
The pilot-in-command may, at his own responsibility, allow any person to enter the
cockpit for purposes other than those mentioned in this Article.
Article llO.Reporting Risks
If the pilot-in-command observes during the flight any unusual weather or malfunction of a
navigational aid or aeronautical systems which might pose danger to the flight, he must report

such conditions to the competent air traffic services (ATS) unit. He must also report promptly
any other conditions that might endanger the safety of the flight.
Article 111.Reporting Aircraft System Failure
The pilot-in-command shall record in the technical log of the aircraft any malfunction or unusual
performance in any of its systems that may occur or is observed during the flight. Prior to each
flight, he must ascertain that action has been taken to address any malfunction or observations
already recorded in the plane's technical log.
Article 112.Guidance to Passengers
a) The operator shall take the necessary measures to ensure that passengers are duly
advised regarding the locations and method of use of seat belts, emergency exits, life
jackets, oxygen masks and other emergency equipment intended for personal or
collective use according to the requirements of the relevant flight.
b) In an emergency during flight, the passengers must be instructed regarding the
emergency measures required under the circumstances.
Article 113.Passengers Boarding while Intoxicated
The operator may not allow a person to board the flight if such a person appeared to be
intoxicated.
PART VIII
COMMERCIAL AIR TRANSPORT AND AERIAL WORK
CHAPTER XIX
CIVIL AVIATION OVERSIGHT
Article 114.Air Transport Policy and Oversight
The Civil Aviation Authority shall establish the commercial air transport policy of the State and
shall assume oversight of this sector in accordance with the public interest. To this end, the
authority shall perform the following duties:
a) Negotiate with other states scheduled and non-scheduled air transport
agreements or any other agreements related to international air transport or
aerial work;
b) Represent the State in international, Arab and African international organizations
concerned with civil aviation and air transport;
c) Participate in and supervise Bilateral or Multilateral Air Service Agreements
between national airlines and foreign airlines to conclude agreements or
arrangements related to joint ventures, code-sharing, royalty or any commercial
or technical operations in accordance with the rules and requirements
established by the Director General;
d) Supervise the commercial air transport activities carried out by airlines of the
State, issue the necessary operating certificates and approve the establishment,
amendment or cancellation of any of its air services or change the number of
flights in accordance with the rules issued by the Director General.

e) Supervise the commercial air transport activities carried out by foreign airlines in
the State, issue the necessary operating certificates and permits and supervise
the exercise by such entities of the traffic rights granted to them. To this end, it
shall inspect the offices of such entities and have access to the necessary
records and documents including oversight on fair trading practices;
f) Authorize national and foreign airlines to operate non-scheduled flights from and
to the territory of the State;
g) Approve tariffs of scheduled and non-scheduled domestic and international air
transport and supervise their implementation, and issue orders regarding such
tariffs; and
h) Suspend or restrict air transport activities of any national or foreign airlines if they
contravene the terms of their operating licenses or permits granted to them, or the
provisions of any bilateral or international agreements concluded with other
States, or any of the provisions of this Proclamation. This provision is without
prejudice to the sanctions and penalties set forth in Part XIV of this Proclamation.
Article 11S.Compliance with the Air Transport Policy
National airlines must adhere to the policy established by the Civil Aviation Authority in
implementation of previous Article of this Proclamation in order to promote and develop
commercial air transport in the State.
Article 116.Exchange and Grant of Air Transport Rights
No agency in the State may conclude agreements, make arrangements or take measures
related to the exchange or grant of air transport rights with any foreign agency except through
the Civil Aviation authority.
Article 117.Conduct of Commercial Air Transport Aerial Work and Ground Services
1. Subject to the provisions of the Convention and other international agreements to which
the State is a party, commercial air transport within the State or abroad may be
undertaken only by the airlines owned by the State or specifically authorized by the State
to conduct such operations.
2. Aerial works or aviation ground services may be carried only with an authorization from
the Civil Aviation Authority.
3. Foreign airlines may maintain an office in the territory of the State only on the basis of
bilateral air transport agreement or authorization from the Civil Aviation Authority, and
within the limits of such an authorization.
4. Foreign airlines may be represented in the territory of the State, whether through a
general agency or other means, only on the basis of a bilateral agreement or an
authorization by the Director General of the Civil Aviation Authority, and within the limits
of the authorization.
5. All national and foreign airlines operating in the territory of the State shall be registered
with the Ministry of Trade and Industry.

6. The Director General shall determine the conditions for granting and revoking the
authorizations referred to in the previous paragraphs and the necessary instructions for
their implementation.
Article US.Cabotage
No foreign aircraft may carry passengers, mail or cargo between two points situated in the
territory of the State. However, the Director General may authorize such transport in cases where
it is in the public interest to do so.
Article U9.Airline Economic and Technical Studies
Prior to operating an air service, national airlines must conduct complete economic and
technical studies for such a service, and present the results to the Civil Aviation Authority which
may either approve, amend or reject.
Article 120.Compliance with Orders
National and foreign airlines shall comply with the orders issued by the Director General,
especially with regard to the following:
CHAPTER XX
PROVISIONS RELATED TO AIRMAIL TRANSPORT
Article 12l.Competence of the Postal Authorities
The competent postal authorities shall supervise the transport of airmail, taking into
consideration the provisions of bilateral air transport agreements and relevant authorizations.
Article 122.Carriage of Airmail
Laws applicable to surface mail shall apply to the transport of airmail unless otherwise
stipulated.

Article 123. Compliance with the International Conventions Related to Airmail Transport
Provisions of international airmail conventions of which the State is a party shall be duly
observed.
Article 124.Duties and Priorities of the Airmail Carrier
1. The air carrier shall transport the airmail as assigned by the postal authorities in
accordance with the postal and air transport regulations in effect.
2. The following priority classification should be adhered to in air transport: passengers and
