their baggage, mail, unaccompanied luggage and cargo.
Article 125.Mail Inspection
Airmail or parcels sent by air may be inspected if the inspector has reason to suspect that any of
such material contains articles that endanger the safety of the aircraft in flight.
No airmail or parcels sent by air may be transported unless they have been received in
accordance with the applicable postal procedures.
PART IX
AVIATION CHARGES
Monetary charges shall be applied for the use of airports and airfields or parts thereof, the
provision of air navigation facilities and services and any other services by the Civil Aviation
Authority or designated, including those given to aircraft, air and ground crew, and flight permits
as well as other related activities. Types and levels of such charges and any exemptions or
reductions shall be determined by the Minister, upon recommendation by the Director General.
PART X
AIRCRAFT ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION
Article 127.Powers and Duties of the Civil Aviation Authority Regarding Aircraft Accidents
and Incidents
a) Conduct a technical investigation of accidents involving civil aircraft in the
territory of the State and accidents involving civil aircraft registered in the State
occurring in the high seas or other the territories that are not under the
jurisdiction of any other state;
b) Submit a report on the circumstances and conditions of each accident or incident
under investigation explaining the probable causes, and publish the results of the
investigation;

c) Develop the necessary recommendations to prevent the recurrence of similar
accidents/incidents, in order to insure the future safety of aviation.
2. If during the investigation and prior to the publication of results, one or more factors have
been identified as a threat to aviation safety, the head of the investigating committee
shall submit relevant recommendations to the Director General to take action as
appropriate.
3. Source of information shall not be liable to prosecution or imposition of any threat
emanating from such an act.
4. The Minister shall establish the necessary systems for accident/incident investigation,
formation of the investigating committees, procedures for the conduct of
accident/incident investigations, reporting, means of removing accident/incident effects
as well as the other rules that should be followed by the competent authorities, flight
crew and other persons when an accident occurs.
Article 128.Aircraft Accident/Incident Reporting
1. If an accident/incident involving an Eritrean-registered aircraft or an aircraft registered in
another state occurs in the territory of the State, the pilot-in-command shall provide the
Director General as soon as possible with information regarding the accident/incident as
required under the rules established by virtue of this Proclamation.
2. In the case of death or incapacitation of the pilot-in-command, such notification shall be
made by the persons to be designated by the Minister for this purpose.
Article 129.Reporting Accidents of Foreign-Registered Aircraft
Upon learning of an accident occurring in the territory of the State involving an aircraft
registered in another state, the Civil Aviation Authority shall notify the following:
1. The State of Registry;
In the event of an accident, the security and competent authorities shall take the following
measures:

Article 131.Formation of Aircraft Accident Investigating Commissions
1. The Director General shall establish commissions to investigate aircraft accidents, which
shall be composed of no less than three members. It may enlist the assistance of
experts, national or foreign, to participate in the investigation in an advisory capacity. The
civil Aviation Authority shall bear the cost of transportation, subsistence allowance and
remuneration of the commission members and advisers. It will also bear the cost of all
air and laboratory tests as well as any technical research required by the circumstances
of the accident.
2. No member of the investigating commiSSion may be removed in the course of the
investigation unless ajustified decision is taken to this effect by the Director General.
Article 132.Terms of Reference of the Investigating Commissions
The members of the investigating commission shall have the right of access to the accident site
and other locations that are of relevance to the investigation. They may inspect such places,
collect samples and have access to records, documents, reference material, charts and papers
and seize those that are deemed relevant to the investigation. They may also summon persons
and call witnesses and require them to submit the information, documents or articles in their
possession, which may be deemed necessary by the commission to determine the facts. They
shall also take the necessary measures to preserve the aircraft, its wreckage, load and parts,
and remove all or any of these to perform any necessary tests.
Article 133.Attendance by a Representative of the State of Registry
If an accident occurs to an aircraft registered in another contracting state occurs in the territory
of the State, the Director General may, under the conditions he deems necessary, allow a
representative from such state to attend the investigation in the capacity of observer. The latter
may be assisted by technical advisers of his choice.
Article 134.Assistance in the Investigation by the Security and Administrative Agencies
The security and administrative agencies, each within their jurisdiction, shall facilitate the work
of the investigation commissions, providing them in particular with all official documents related
to the accident. They shall carry out rescue and first aid operations, removal of casualties, fire-
fighting and removal of bodies. They shall preserve the site and follow all instructions given by
the investigation commissions to facilitate its work.
Article 135.Report of the Investigating Commission
1. At the end of the investigation, the investigating commission shall prepare its report on
the accident, including its causes and the circumstances surrounding it, the conclusions
of the investigation and the evidence and the essential information which formed the
basis of such conclusions, as well as its recommendations. The report shall be promptly
submitted to the Minister.

2. If the investigation involves an accident involving an aircraft registered in another
Contracting State, the Director General shall, as soon as possible, send a copy of the
report to the State of Registry and the state of the Operator. It may send the report or
some of its parts to:
c) Any other state which was duly notified in accordance with Article 129 of this
Proclamation, or which has an essential interest in the conclusions of the
investigation which are contained in the report.
3. Reports on incidents may be communicated in accordance with the relevant provisions
of this Proclamation.
4. Individuals or agencies may receive copies of the accident reports in accordance with
the decisions setting forth the terms and procedures for obtaining such reports as well as
the relevant charges.
Article 136.Accidents Caused by a Criminal Act
If the investigating commission establishes that the accident has been caused by sabotage or a
suspected offence, it shall advise the Attorney General's Office in order to take the necessary
legal action in this respect.
Article 137.Assignment ofAccident Investigators Abroad
In case of an accident involving an aircraft registered in the State occurs abroad, the Civil
Aviation Authority may, immediately after the occurrence, dispatch its aircraft accident
investigation officials.
Article 138.Accident Investigation by a Contracting State
If an investigation of an accident occurring outside the territory of the State is conducted by
another state, the Director General shall provide that state, upon request, with whatever
information he can obtain in respect of the accident, including information relating to aviation
safety and its services that may have been used prior to the accident, provided that the
investigating state, if it is so requested, allows the representative appointed by the Director
General to participate in the investigation.
Article 139.Authenticity of the Facts in the Final Report
The facts contained in the final report of the investigating commission in an aircraft accident
shall be considered accurate until proven otherwise.
The Director General may decide to re-open investigation in an aircraft accident indicating the
reasons for such decision, if new and significant evidence appears that might affect the outcome
of the investigation.
Article 140.Joint Investigation Commissions
The Minister, in coordination with the competent military authorities, shall establish the
regulations governing accidents in the territory of the State involving a military aircraft and one
or more civil aircraft. Such regulations shall also address the accidents of civil aircraft occurring

at military airports and zones. The Minister shall establish an investigating commission
composed of an equal number of representatives of the Civil Aviation Authority and the
competent military authorities for this purpose as deemed appropriate.
PART XX
SEARCH AND RESCUE
Article 141.Search and Rescue Organization
1. The Director General shall establish the search and rescue areas for which the State is
responsible; such areas shall be announced by the Civil Aviation Authority.
2. The Director General shall organize rescue units in collaboration with the competent
authorities. Such units shall always be ready to intervene in accordance with the
established plan.
3. The Civil Aviation Authority shall take the necessary measures to coordinate and
cooperate with others states, particularly neighboring ones, on matters related to search
and rescue.
Article 142.0bligation to Render Search and Rescue Assistance
1. No person or agency shall refrain from rendering search and rescue assistance within its
power upon request of the competent authorities.
2. The obligation set forth in paragraph (1) above shall apply to persons and agencies
whose nature of work places them in a position to render such assistance.
Article 143.Access to Prohibited Areas for Search and Rescue Purposes
The competent authorities shall allow access by persons, equipment and aircraft engaged in
search and rescue to enter any prohibited or restricted area if a probability exists that the
distressed aircraft is present in that area. Such operations shall be conducted under the
supervision of the competent authorities.
Article 144.Entering the State for Search and Rescue Purposes
The competent authorities shall allow immediate and temporary entry of experts, equipment and
aircraft that the Civil Aviation Authority deems necessary for search and rescue operations in the
State to take part in such operations.
Article 145.Preserving the Scene of the Accident
During the conduct of the rescue operations, no person may move any part or component of an
aircraft involved in an accident, nor deform any of the evidence of the accident unless it is
required for the rescue operations or if done with an authorization by the Civil Aviation Authority.
The search and rescue guard and control units shall implement these measures, pending
completion of information necessary for the accident investigation.
Article 146.Compensation and Cost Recovery of Search and Rescue Operations
1. Any person who has rendered any search and rescue assistance may, in accordance
with the provisions of this Part, recover the cost of such assistance and may receive

compensation for any damage sustained during such operations or as a direct result
thereof.
2. The provisions of the previous paragraph shall not apply to any assistance provided by
public authorities in the State.
Article 147.Search and Rescue Remunerations
In addition to the costs and compensations provided for inArticle 144, the Director General shall
establish the regulations governing the disbursement of search and rescue remuneration of
persons, aircraft and property onboard, including mail shipments subsequent to approval
granted by the Minister.
Article 148.Liability of the Operator of Distressed Aircraft
The operator of a distressed aircraft shall pay the cost of the search and rescue assistance as
well as the damages and remunerations even when the aircraft in question is owned by the
assistance provider.
Article 149.Competent Court in Search and Rescue Claims
The court in the jurisdiction where the accident took place shall have the authority to consider
claims arising from search and rescue. The Eritrean courts shall have jurisdiction over the case
if the accident takes place over the high seas or at a location that is not subject to the
sovereignty of any State in the following cases:
1. If the aircraft subject of the search and rescue operations is registered in the
State;
2. If the aircraft subject of the search and rescue is present following an accident in
the territory of the State, and the plaintiff is a citizen of the State.
Article 1S0.Statute of Limitation on Search and Rescue Claims
Claims arising from search and rescue shall expire two years after the end of the search and
rescue operation. In case the statute ceases or is suspended, such claims will not be receivable
three years after the termination of the search and rescue operation.
PART XXI
RESPONSIBILITIES AND GUARANTEES RELATING
TO AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS
CHAPTER XXI
CONTRACTUAL LIABILITY IN AIR TRANSPORT
Article 151.Liability in International and Domestic Operations
1. In respect of liability in international air transport, the provisions of any international
convention on the unification of certain rules of international air transport, to which the
State is a signatory party, shall be applied.
2. In respect of domestic air transport, the relevant rules and provisions set forth in the
applicable legislation in force shall apply.

The carrier shall not be liable to consignors or consignees if the cargo onboard had to be
dropped in flight for the survival of the aircraft, provided the carrier and his subordinates have
taken the necessary measures to avoid the damage, or if it was impossible to take such
measures.
Article 153.Lack of Carrier Liability Regarding Disembarked Passengers
The carrier shall not be liable if the pilot-in-command was forced to require the disembarkation
of any disruptive passenger or a passenger who posed a threat to the safety of the aircraft or its
passengers.
Article 154.Ascertaining the Presence of Travel Documents
Each air carrier shall insure that passengers and cargo carry the documents required for entry
into the territory of the State or departure therefrom to the airport of destination; otherwise the
carrier shall bear the consequences of its negligence.
CHAPTER XXII
DAMAGE CAUSED BY AIRCRAFT TO A THIRD PARTY ON THE SURFACE
Article 155. Provisions Related to the Damage Caused by Aircraft to a Third Party on the
Surface
The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to any damage caused by an aircraft to a third party
on the surface in the territory of the State unless the State is a party to any relevant international
convention.
Article 156.Compensation for any Damage Caused by Aircraft to Third Parties on the
Surface
Any person who sustains damage on the surface is entitled to compensation once it is
established that such damage was directly caused by an aircraft in flight or by a person or
object falling from such aircraft.
Except for the cases indicated in this Article, the general rules in force in the State shall apply,
and the aircraft operator shall be liable for the damage mentioned in this Article.
Article 157.Joint Liability in case an Aircraft is Used Without the Consent of its Operator
If a person uses an aircraft without the consent of its operator, and unless the operator
establishes that he has taken necessary care to avoid such use, he shall be jointly liable with
the person who used the aircraft without its consent for any justifiable damages as stipulated in
Article 156. Each of them shall be liable within the limits specified in that Chapter.
Article 158. Exemption and Reduction of Compensation
The person responsible for the damage shall not be liable if the damage was directly the result
of armed conflict or internal unrest of if he is prevented from using the aircraft by order of the
public authorities, or if the damage was the result of fault, negligence or abstention by the
person who suffered the damage or his subordinates or agents.

If the responsible person proves that the person who suffered the damage or his subordinates
or agents contributed to the incidence of the damage, the compensation shall be reduced
proportionately to such contribution.
Exemption from paying compensation or reduction of the compensation is not allowed in case of
a fault by the subordinates or agents of the person who sustained the damage if it is established
that they were acting beyond the limits of their powers.
Article 159. Damage Caused by Several Aircraft
If the damage to a third party on the surface is caused by a collision between two or more
aircraft in flight or because one impeded the movement of another, or if this damage is caused
by two or more aircraft, each aircraft shall be deemed as having caused the damage and the
operator of each aircraft shall be jointly liable for damages in accordance with the provisions of
this Proclamation.
Article 160.Multiple Liability for Damage
If several persons are responsible for the damage under this Proclamation, the persons
sustaining the damage are only entitled to the damages that may be ruled on one person.
Article 161.Competent Courts
Claims for compensation for damage caused by aircraft to third parties on the surface in the
State shall be brought before the competent court in the place of occurrence, the place of
residence of the plaintiff or his principle place of business.
Article 162.Statute of Limitation
Claims for compensation for damage caused by aircraft to third parties on the surface shall
expire after two years from the date of the occurrence. In case the statute ceases or is
suspended no such claims shall be receivable three years from the date of the occurrence.
Article 163.Damage Resulting from Aircraft Engine Noise, Vibrations and Emissions
No right to compensation may be established for any damage resulting from aircraft engine
noise, vibrations or emissions if the operation is conducted in accordance with the provisions of
this Proclamation and its executive regulations.
CHAPTER XXIII
INSURANCE AND GUARANTEES REQUIRED TO COVER
LIABILITIES RELATED TO AIRCRAFT OPERATION
Article 164.Insurance Coverage by the Operator
Subject to the provisions of this Proclamation, each operator of an aircraft operating in the
territory of the State shall be insured to cover liability for damage to the passengers, luggage
and cargo on board the aircraft, as well as damage caused by the aircraft to third parties on the
surface. Each such operator shall also insure its staff against any damage caused by aviation
risks.

Article165.Placement of Insurance with an Authorized Insurer
The insurance prescribed in the above Article shall be taken out with an insurer authorized to
engage in insurance activities under the laws of the State of Registry.
Article 166.Guarantees Instead of Insurance
The insurance coverage referred to in Article 164 may be replaced by any of the following
guarantees:
1. Depositing a cash security with the treasury of the State of Registry or a bank so
authorized by that State;
2. Submission of a security from a bank so authorized by the State of Registry,
provided that State verifies the operator's ability to fulfill its obligations;
3. Submission of a security from the State of Registry subject to an undertaking by
that State to refrain from invoking any judicial immunity in case of a dispute over
such security.
In all cases, the above-mentioned guarantees shall be within the limits established by the
Minister by virtue of international conventions.
Article 167.Carriage of Insurance Document On Board Aircraft or Filing a Copy thereof
with the Civil Aviation Authority
The Civil Aviation Authority may require any aircraft operating in the territory of the State to carry
on board a certificate issued by an insurer certifying that the insurance coverage has been
taken, in accordance with the provisions of this Proclamation, as well as a certificate from the
competent authority in the State of Registry or the state where the insurer has its residence or
principal place of business confirming the operator's solvency.
The carriage of the above-mentioned certificates onboard aircraft may be replaced by filing
certified copies thereof with the Civil Aviation Authority.
PART XXII
OFFENCES AGAINST SECURITY
AND SAFETY OF AVIATION AND AIRPORTS
CHAPTER XXIII
OFFENCES AGAINST THE SAFETY
OF CIVIL AVIATION
Article 168.Determination of Offences against the Safety of Civil Aviation
1. Any person commits an offence if he unlawfully and intentionally:
a) performs an act of violence against a person on board an aircraft in flight if that
act is likely to endanger the safety of that aircraft; or

b) destroys an ain::raft in service or causes damage to such an aircraft which
renders it incapable of flight or which is likely to endanger its safety in flight; or
c) destroys or damages air navigation facilities or interferes with their operation, if
any such act is likely to endanger the safety of aircraft in flight; or
d) communicates information which he knows to be false, thereby endangering the
safety of an aircraft in flight.
e) Steals air navigation equipment or any other equipment, systems or cables that
are necessary to ensure the safety of the aviation or related thereto.
2. Any person also commits an offence if he intentionally and unlawfully uses any device,
substance or weapon:
a) to perform an act of violence against any person in a civil airport if such an act
caused or is likely to cause serious injury or death;
b) to perform an act of violence against a person at a civil airport if such an act
disrupts or impedes any of the ongoing operations at the airport or causes panic
at that airport;
c) to destroy or cause serious damage to airport facilities or to an aircraft not in
service at the airport, or cause interruption in the services of the airport if such an
act causes or is likely to cause danger to safety at the airport.
a) attempts to commit any of the offences mentioned in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this
Article.
b) is an accomplice of a person who commits or attempts to commit any such
offence.
Article 169.Definition of "in flight" and "in service"
For the purposes of this Part:
1, An aircraft is considered to be in flight at any time from the moment when all its external
doors are closed following embarkation of passengers until the moment when any such
door is opened for disembarkation. In case of a forced landing, the flight shall be
deemed to continue until the competent authorities take over the responsibility for the
aircraft and for the persons and property on board.
2, An aircraft is considered to be in service from the beginning of the preflight preparation
of the aircraft by ground personnel or by the crew for a specific flight until twenty-four
hours after any landing; the period of service shall, in any event, extend for the entire
period during which the aircraft is in flight as defined in paragraph (1) of this Article.

CHAPTER XXIV
OFFENCES OF UNLAWFUL SEIZURE OF AIRCRAFT
Article 170.Determination of Offences of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft
Any person commits an offence if he on board an aircraft in flight:
1. unlawfully, by force or threat thereof, or by any other form of intimidation, seizes,
or exercises control of, that aircraft, or attempts to perform any such act, or
2. is an accomplice of a person who performs any of the acts referred to in the
previous paragraph.
Article 171.Definition of Aircraft in Flight
For the purposes of this Chapter, an aircraft is considered to be in flight according to the
meaning indicated inArticle 169, paragraph 1.
CHAPTER XXV
POWERS OF THE PllOT-IN-COMMAND AND CREW
Article 172.Preventive Measures
The pilot-in-command may, when he has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has
committed, or is about to commit, on board the aircraft, any of the offences provided for in this
Part or any act which he believes will endanger the safety of the aircraft, impose upon such
person any necessary or preventive measures including restraint. The pilot-in-command may
require or authorize the assistance of other crew members and may request or authorize, but
not require, the assistance of passengers for this purpose.
1. The pilot-in-command may request the authorities of the state in the territory of which the
aircraft lands, to disembark the person referred to in the above Article, giving the
reasons for such disembarkation.
2. If the pilot-in-command intends to deliver the person because of the seriousness of the
offence, he shall as soon as practicable notify the authorities of the state in the territory
of which the aircraft lands of his intention to deliver such person and the reasons thereof.
The pilot-in-command shall upon landing submit a report including any evidence and any
information in his possession.
Article 174.Responsibility for Preventive Measures
In respect of the measures taken in accordance with Article 172, the responsibility of the pilot-
in-command, any member of its crew or passengers, the aircraft owner or operator or the
person on whose account the aircraft is being operated, shall not be invoked in any claim arising
from the treatment of a person against whom such measures have been taken.

CHAPTER XXVI
POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE STATE
Article 175.Regaining Control over the Aircraft and Allowing the Passengers to Continue
their Journey
In case of an act to commit, attempt to commit, or participate in committing, any of the offences
referred to in Articles 168 and 170, or an act that might endanger the safety of the aircraft, the
competent authorities shall take the necessary measures to restore control of the aircraft to its
pilot, or to maintain his control thereon. In such cases, the passengers and crew of an aircraft
that has landed in the territory of the State shall be allowed to continue their journey as soon as
practicable. The competent authorities shall also return the aircraft and its cargo to the persons
lawfully entitled to possession.
Article 176. Jurisdiction
1. The State shall establish itsjurisdiction over the offences mentioned in Articles 168 and
b) when the offence is committed against or on board an aircraft registered in the
State;
c) when the aircraft on board which the offence is committed lands in the territory of
the State with the alleged offender still on board;
d) when the offence is committed against or on board an aircraft leased without
crew to a lessee who has his principal place of business or, if the lessee has no
such place of business, his permanent residence, in the State.
2. However, in case any of the offences referred to in Article 168, (1), a), b) and c) to an
aircraft in flight, the State shall have jurisdiction over any such offence.
Article 177.Jurisdiction in Case of International or Joint Registration
If the State has established joint air transport operating organizations or international operating
agencies, which operate aircraft which are subject to joint or international registration, the Civil
Aviation Authority of the State shall designate, in agreement with such states, the state which
shall exercise the jurisdiction and assume the functions of the State of Registry in respect of the
provisions of this Proclamation.
Article 178.Disembarkation of the Suspect
The competent authorities shall allow the pilot-in-command to disembark any person in
accordance with Article 173.
Article 179.Legal Measures
The competent authorities shall take into custody any person who is handed over to them by the
pilot-in-command in accordance with Article 173. If the offender is present in the territory of the
State of Eritrea or if he has been handed over by the pilot-in-command, the competent
authorities shall promptly investigate the incident.

If the competent authorities conclude that the offence falls within the jurisdiction of the State of
Eritrea in accordance with Article 175, they shall take the necessary measures to submit the
case to the competent court.
If the competent authorities conclude that the offence does not fall within the jurisdiction of the
State, they may take action as appropriate under the law, and in accordance with the
international conventions of which the State is a party. In all cases, the competent authorities of
the State may refuse to take custody of the offender or deport him or extradite him to the state of
which he is a national or to the state of which he is a permanent resident or the state in the
territory of which he commenced his journey.
Article l80.CiviJ Aviation Security and Safety
The competent authorities shall coordinate with the Civil Aviation Authority in taking the
necessary preventive measures against any acts or offences that may be committed against the
security and safety of civil aviation in the State and which may be committed on board civil
aircraft, in accordance with the relevant international rules and the provisions of this
Proclamation.
PART XXIII
SANCTIONS AND PENALTIES
Article l81.Vioiations of Aerial Easement Rights
Any person who commits any of the provisions of Articles 23, 25 or 26 of this Proclamation shall
be punishable by a maximum prison term of 2 years or a maximum fine of 10,000 (ten
thousand) Nakfa or both.
Article l82.Violation of Commercial Transport Provisions
A monetary fine of 10,000 (ten thousand) Nakfa or a prison term of two years shall be imposed
on any operator or air carrier or any of their agents who operates an aircraft without prior
authorization or in contravention with the air transport authorization granted thereto or the orders
issued in accordance with the provisions of this Proclamation. The Civil Aviation Authority shall
be entitled to a compensation equal to double the amount of the fare obtained by any airline or
air transport enterprise affiliated to another State, in contravention of the bilateral air services
agreements concluded between the State of Eritrea and the State of the airline or enterprise that
violated the provisions of the authorizations issued thereto, if such violation is related to any of
the provisions of commercial air transport.
Article l83.Punishment ofActs Endangering Flight Safety
A prison term of two years or a maximum fine of 10,000 (ten thousand) Nakfa or both shall be
imposed on any person who commits any of the following acts:
1. engages in flying or operating an aircraft that does not carry any nationality or
registration marks or carries false or unclear marks, without a special
authorization by the Director General;
2. engages in flying an aircraft over a prohibited area, or if he is unintentionally
located over any such area and did not comply with the orders issued to him;

3. operates an aircraft prior to obtaining its certificate of registration or certificate of
airworthiness without a special authorization. The aircraft operator shall also be
liable to the same penalty if he is aware of such offence.
Article 184.Punishment of Acts for Flight Procedure violations
A maximum prison term of two years or a maximum fine of 10,000 (ten thousand) Nakfa or both

Article 185.Unauthorized Transport of Dangerous Goods

Article 186.Carriage of Persons for the Purpose of Smuggling or Committing an Offence
A prison term of two years or a fine of 10,000 (ten thousand) Nakfa or both shall be imposed on
any person who transports other persons on board an aircraft with the purpose of engaging in
smuggling operations or in committing an offence, even if such an offence is not actually
committed.
Article 187.Practicing without Authorization
A maximum prison term of one year or a maximum fine of 5,000 (five thousand) Nakfa or both
shall be imposed on any person who performs without a license, certificate, qualification or
permit, or who fails to be bound by the conditions therein.
Article 188.Flying an Aircraft while Intoxicated
A maximum prison term of three years or a maximum fine of 10,000 (ten thousand) Nakfa or
both shall be imposed on any person who flies an aircraft while intoxicated or under the
influence of narcotics or psychotropic substances.
A prison term of five years or a maximum fine of 10,000 (ten thousand) Nakfa or both shall be
imposed on any person who intentionally fails to record the data that the operator or his
subordinates are required to enter in the aircraft documents and records, or intentionally
changes data or enters false information therein.
Article 190.Unauthorized Access
A maximum prison term of three years or a fine of 10,000 (ten thousand) Nakfa or both on any
person who enters without authorization an area where access is prohibited by the airport
regulations or instructions, or who leaves animals or objects in such areas.

Article 193.Penalties Imposed by the Director General
Without prejudice to any provision of this Proclamation, the Director General may suspend or
revoke any license, certificate, permit, authorization or approval, or withdraw any approval
granted, issued or endorsed under this Proclamation and its implementing rules and regulations.
Article 194.Prevention, Suspension or Removal of Violations
Without prejudice to the provisions of the previous Article, the Director General shall take the
necessary measures to prevent, suspend or remove violations of Articles 25, 27 and 28 while
requiring the violator to pay all charges and fees incurred by the State in this respect.
Article 195.Seizure ofAircraft or Preventing Departure ofAircraft
·1. The Director General may impose precautionary seizure on national or foreign aircraft if
they do not comply with the conditions of this Proclamation and the regulations and
decisions issued hereunder. Such seizure shall continue until the relevant conditions
have been complied with.
2. The Director General may also prevent the departure of any aircraft if reasonable ground
exists to justify or prove that the conditions are not suitable for the flight, or it violates the
provisions of this Proclamation.
Article 196.Suspension or Revocation of a License if a Judgment is Rendered in a Criminal
Case
A guilty sentence in a crime or a dishonorable offence shall result in the suspension of a license
issued or validated by the Director General for a period to be determined in the judgment. It may
also be revoked if a sentence is rendered in a criminal case or a case involving a dishonorable
offence.
Article 197.Enforcement of More Stringent Punishment
The provisions of this Proclamation shall be without prejudice to any more stringent penalties
provided for in the Penal Code of Eritrea or other applicable Laws.

Article 198.Jurisdiction
Eritrean courts shall have jurisdiction over offences against the provisions of this Proclamation,
or the decisions, rules and regulations issued for application thereof, if such offences have been
committed in the territory of the State of Eritrea, or on board Eritrean registered aircraft in flight
over the high seas or in locations that are not under the jurisdiction of any other State.
Article 199.Confiscation of an Aircraft
An aircraft may be confiscated by a court ruling in the following cases:
1. If the aircraft carries incorrect nationality or registration marks, or if it does not
carry any such marks;
2. If the aircraft owner or operator transports weapons or ammunition with the
purpose of smuggling or committing an offence against the security of the State.
Article 200.Actions for which no Penalty is Provided under the Law
Any person who commits an act prohibited under this Proclamation or abstains from an action
required under its provisions and for which no penalty has been provided under this
Proclamation or in other laws, shall be liable of a maximum prison term of five years or a
maximum fine of 50,000 (fifty thousand) Nakfa or both.
PART XXIV
MILITARY AIRCRAFT
Article 201.Compliance with Rules of the Air
All military aircraft shall comply with the rules of the air as contained in this Proclamation and
the regulations and decisions issued hereunder, while in flight or transit in controlled airspace or
using civil airports.
Article 202.0ver-flight of Foreign Military Aircraft in the State
No foreign military aircraft may fly within the territory of the State or land therein unless it is
authorized to do so by virtue of an international convention or agreement of which the State is a
party, or by special authorization by the competent authorities. Such aircraft must display their
marks clearly. The Authority requesting permission for flight must also pay charges for the
services rendered in accordance with current tariff and rates approved by the CAA of the State.
Arrears exceeding six Months shall be charged an extra 10% - 30% of the amount invoiced.
Moreover, operators requesting for amendment of flight permit shall be charged an extra 5% of
the amount invoiced.
Article 203. Exclusions
The provisions of this Proclamation and its executing regulations and decisions, especially
those related to aircraft in current use, shall apply to all other aircraft, unless this is rendered
impossible due to the nature, structure, technical or economic importance of such aircraft, as

determined by the Director General, or where they are covered by a special provision elsewhere
in this Proclamation or other laws and regulations.
Article 204.Executing Decisions and Regulations
The executing regulations of this Proclamation shall be issued by the Director General.

this Proclamation may seek a review by the High Court of Eritrea within 30 days of such
a decision.
